questions.q: What is the purpose of the hydrogel modification in the zinc iodine battery?
questions.answer: To ensure that when zinc accumulates on the anode side, it does so evenly, mitigating the shuttle effect and accelerating the iodine conversion reaction on the cathode side.

questions.q: What is the shuttle effect in batteries?

triples.o: diffusion of polysulfide between anode and cathode

questions.q: What functional groups does the hydrogel have on the anode and cathode sides?
questions.answer: The anode side has zincophilic functional groups (affinity for zinc) and the cathode side has iodophilic functional groups (affinity for iodine).

questions.q: How does the hydrogel electrolyte affect polyiodides on the anode side?
questions.answer: It repels dissolved polyiodides, allowing zinc to be deposited uniformly and protecting the anode from iodine-caused corrosion.

questions.q: How does the hydrogel electrolyte affect redox reactions on the cathode side?
questions.answer: It immobilizes polyiodides at the cathode side and speeds up redox reactions thanks to synchronized rapid transport of ions and electrons.

questions.q: How does the solid nature of the hydrogel electrolyte limit dendrite growth?
questions.answer: Its mechanical strength acts as a physical barrier not present in liquid electrolytes.
